slides.text:
what avoiding one client email
looks like with adhd

i open it. read it. close it.

14 tabs open.

at night i write the whole

then i tapped to break it into tiny steps.

instagram.caption:
What avoiding one client email looks like with ADHD.

I opened it and closed it six times a day. I wrote the whole reply in my head at night. It sat there for three days.

What helped: I said the task out loud to FOCO and tapped once to break it into tiny steps. Step 1 was just "open the email." I set a 5-minute timer. The reply took 12 minutes.

Save this for the next email you can't make yourself answer.
instagram.altText: Nine-slide photo story. Five nighttime photos show someone avoiding one client email: a woman at her laptop in the dark, a glowing screen, a desk at night, a bedside clock reading 4:08, someone lying awake in bed. Then three screens from the FOCO app: recording the task by voice, the task broken into small steps, and a 5-minute focus timer. The last photo is in daylight: a woman at a sunny window with her laptop, reply sent.
